newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Argentina president visits his troops in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Argentina president visits his troops in Cyprus.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem spent his country's army day anniversary in Cyprus on Wednesday with Argentine troops of the United Nations Peacekeeping Force on the divided island, UNFICYP.

"I hope that the peace that will be here in the future will not depend on the presence of the blue helmets but will be the result of the agreements that will be reached among the peoples of this world," Menem told a ceremony held to commemorate the creation of the army in Argentina.

Menem, speaking to Argentine peacekeepers and their families at San Martin camp, a pine valley in the foothills of the Troodos mountains some 40 km west of the Cypriot capital Nicosia, praised the men and women of the force for their service to their country.

Accompanied by army chief of staff Martin Antonio Balza and several cabinet members, Menem took the salute of troops who patrol the western part of the 180 km-long buffer zone separating the two communities of the island.
Argentina is the largest troop contributor to the 1166-strong UNFICYP, with 389 soldiers. Britain follows with 388.

The buffer zone has separated the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities of Cyprus since Turkey invaded the north in 1974 in response to a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the military ruling Greece.
